thread:
violet: Noticed a reproducible pause in onboarding sampleapp around token rotation + pagination. SDK clamps client window to 1 and paginator backs up. No 429s upstream but users see ~5s freeze. Anyone else?

sam: Which paginator variant?

violet: The adaptive prefetching one. Repro: 6 clients, pageSize=40, force refresh ~6s in. Window goes from ~7 to 1 after refresh and requests queue.

priya: That clamp was meant as a safe fallback, but it's too aggressive. It interacts poorly with prefetch buffer refill.

violet: Condensed logs:
[2026-03-22T11:02:10Z] fetchPage(c=1,p=5) -> 200 latency=110ms
[2026-03-22T11:02:16Z] auth:refresh(c=1) -> 200
[2026-03-22T11:02:16Z] window.adjust(c=1) old=7 new=1 reason=auth_event
[2026-03-22T11:02:16Z] enqueue(c=3,p=6) queued=4 wait=3.8s

sam: Sounds like control-loop oscillation: clamp -> buffer drains -> aggressive refill -> queueing.

priya: Proposed fixes: (A) on successful auth refresh, don't drop below max(2, ceil(old*0.25)). (B) scale prefetch target to current window to avoid over-requesting.

sam: Also add fast-path: if auth refresh is 2xx and next N requests have <5% errors, ramp back up with jitter instead of waiting long decay.

ci-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-9452 "sdk: reduce auth clamp to avoid prefetch stalls" and attached logs.

violet: I'll add a deterministic integration test that simulates token TTL expiry mid-iteration with 6 clients and asserts average queue time <3s.

priya: I'll draft the heuristic change and an env var toggle SDK_PREFETCH_SCALE for experimentation. Add a doc note to onboarding: "token rotation can trigger client-side backpressure; for heavy pagination prefer refresh margin >30s during load tests."

sam: After patches land run sampleapp-load (https://ci.internal/redwood/sampleapp-load) and watch per-client wait histograms. If spikes remain we can relax clamp or add a short grace window post-refresh.

violet: Thanks — will post PRs and CI links here. :thumbsup:
